Camping Overview in WoW Forever

Experience Food Buffs in WoW Forever

At BlizzCon's WoW Forever Deep Dive, developer Josh Greenfield (Aggrend) breaks down the importance of the Campfire feature in WoW Forever. In this breakdown, we learned about new additions to food buffs: the Well Fed XP Boost. So, along with getting a buff that awards +Strength, Stamina, Intellect, or other stats, there will also be an additional +5% Experience gained with it.

contentHtml:
The announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever sent shockwaves through the gaming industry, but for players actively playing a mode like The Burning Crusade Anniversary, one question lingered: How will this affect the game?

World of Warcraft: Forever Podcast & Brewfest in This Week's WoW Weekly


With WoW Forever not set to launch until Nov. 4 and instant, guaranteed Beta access behind a $60 bundle, it might've been fair to assume TBC Anniversary would still have a strong raiding population through at least WoW Forever's November launch. However, after just one week of the WoW Forever Beta, we're already seeing massive chunks of the raiding player base dissipate.

Additional WoW: Forever Collector's Editions Available


According to Ironforge.pro, which pulls raid log data from Warcraft Logs, TBC Anniversary had a raiding player base of 212,821 the week of Sept. 8 through Sept. 14. The following week, from Sept. 15 to Sept. 21, that number plummeted to 124,487. That's a drop-off of 88,334 raiders. Right now, TBC Anniversary is in Phase 3: Black Temple and Mount Hyjal. Zul'Aman and Sunwell Plateau are still to come.



From there, it's unclear if there are plans to go into Wrath of the Lich King Anniversary. In addition to the TBC Anniversary players, the Mists of Pandaria Classic player base is also awaiting insight into what will happen to their characters, which have been with them since WoW Classic launched in August 2019. Speaking of Mists of Pandaria Classic, that raiding player base fell from 33,125 to 24,971 with the launch of the WoW Forever Beta. In MOP Classic, that version of the game has been in its final phase since June, with the launch of Siege of Orgrimmar.



With their futures uncertain and no clear progression path, this data suggests players are either playing the WoW Forever Beta or waiting to hear what Blizzard plans for both game modes.

title.en: Recent Allies Feature in WoW: Forever Helps with a Sense of Community
title.es: Función de aliados recientes en WoW: Forever ayuda con un sentido de comunidad

summary.en: Recent Allies Feature in WoW: Forever Helps with a Sense of Community...
summary.es: Función de aliados recientes en WoW: Forever ayuda con un sentido de comunidad...

contentHtml:
WoW: Forever has added a new Recent Allies feature that can help you remember familiar faces!

World of Warcraft: Forever places a strong emphasis on social features. Blizzard has discussed the idea of friction and how that leads to a more social experience in recent interviews. The Game Informer Interview highlights that some inconveniences, such as running to a dungeon or a long flight path, can actually lead to players being more social.

Similarly, in the Windows Central Interview, Blizzard noted that reducing friction tends to end up with a more solitary experience, whereas friction typically leads to more social connections. This can be seen in the lack of shared mob tagging, which incentivizes players to group up.

With this in mind, WoW: Forever includes the Recent Allies window as a feature.

 


Every time you group with a player in WoW: Forever, their record gets saved in the Recent Allies pane. This saves their name, current level, class, the location where you interacted, and what activity you did together. If they are online, there's a one-click invite button as well!

In addition, you can also pin some of your recent allies so that they're always listed at the top of the window. If you play with them enough, maybe you'll invite them to your friends list instead!

 


The Recent Allies pane, as an extension of the Friends List, could be useful in a game that is focusing on the social experience. Whether you're questing and grouping to take down a dangerous enemy, or grouping for a dungeon, your Recent Allies list will be full of players as you adventure through Azeroth. Maybe you find that one person who is always down to do a dungeon with you, or a person who always seems to be in the same questing areas. Reach out, and maybe you'll make a new friend in the process!

contentHtml:
Blizzard has revealed the Bonus Reward for completing the October 2026 Traveler's Log!

In today's WoW Weekly, Blizzard recapped the last week of World of Warcraft, while also revealing something new for the future. The October 2026 Trading Post's bonus reward is Ensemble: Thornshadow Assassin's Attire!

 
Blizzard
View Original

Dress to Distress with Costumed Calamity in October’s Trading Post

This Month's Bonus Reward: Thornshadow Assassin's Attire Transmog Set
“For missions that don't officially exist.”
October’s Trading Post is cloaked in calamity, with fiendish finds ready to add chaos to your collection. Complete activities to earn Trader’s Tender, fill your Traveler’s Log, and slink into the shadows with the Ensemble: Thornshadow Assassin's Attire.

Visit T&W (Tawney and Wilder) just outside the Mage District in Stormwind, or the Zen’shiri Trading Post next to Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, to check out the latest items they have available. Players can also visit the Trading Post in the capital cities of Dornogal (The Foregrounds) on the Isle of Dorn and in the renewed Silvermoon City, where representatives of both Tawney and Wilder and the Zen’shiri Trading Post are open for business.

Champions new to or returning to World of Warcraft and Midnight can tour the Trading Post to learn everything you need to know, from where to find it to how you can earn additional Trader's Tender through the Traveler's Log.

The September Trading Post Outlet closes soon! Get in your last purchases before the vendors change over to their October inventory.

contentHtml:
Blizzard has posted this week's WoW Weekly which includes the first episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Brewfest and more!
Blizzard
View Original
There’s more to discover in World of Warcraft: Forever. This week, dig into our latest articles covering your first choices in a reimagined original Azeroth—from choosing your ruleset and naming your character to exploring class and race combinations, the new Skyborne race, and the Legacy System—then watch episode 1 of the World of Warcraft: Forever Podcast. You can also look ahead to October’s Trading Post and catch up on the Brewfest in-game holiday, what’s happening in the WoW Portal Room, and more in WoW Weekly.

Watch the World of Warcraft: Forever Podcast, Ep. 1

Join Senior Game Designer Josh “Aggrend” Greenfield, Lead Classic Designer Tim Jones, and content creators Countdown To Classic and Xaryu in the first episode of the World of Warcraft: Forever Podcast.

Get to Know World of Warcraft: Forever

Catch up on the latest from World of Warcraft: Forever, including choosing your ruleset, naming your character, class and race combinations, the Skyborne, and the Legacy System as you prepare to carve your path through Azeroth.
Choose Your Ruleset
Every journey through Azeroth begins with a choice about the kind of world you want to step into. In World of Warcraft: Forever, rulesets help you choose the kind of experience you want first as you begin carving your path through Azeroth. All you need to know is in our overview.
Create a Name of Your Own
A name is one of the first choices you make when creating a character. In World of Warcraft: Forever, character names gain more room to breathe through a new two-name structure designed for a larger, realmless Azeroth. More details can be found here.
Create the Hero You Want to Be
Race and class shape the hero you become, from the fantasy you embody to the role you take on in the world. You can return to a familiar favorite, explore a newly available combination, or begin your journey as a Skyborne character, with each choice offering a different way to step into Azeroth’s next chapter. Your hero awaits—learn more about it in our article.
Meet the New Skyborne
A new adventure rises above Azeroth. The Skyborne invite you into a story of wind and ancestry—one that begins on Zephras Isle and continues as you decide whether your Skyborne will join the Horde or the Alliance. Learn more about the Skyborne here.
Get to Know the Legacy System
Take a peek at an account-wide horizontal progression system—the Legacy System. It’s a way to progress by exploring more of what the game has to offer, while every character you love contributes to your journey. Learn more about this feature here.

Raise Your Stein! Brewfest Returns with Battle-Brewed Rewards

Eat delicious food, drink bountiful beverages, and ride rams around barrels of apples! Brewfest has arrived, and you can enjoy all that and more!

When : September 20–October 6
Where : Silvermoon City, Valdrakken, Dornogal, Valdrakken, Ironforge, and Orgrimmar
Currency : Brewfest Prize Tokens—used to purchase most items at the Brewfest vendor.

Strike up a conversation with the Holiday Enthusiast in Silvermoon City to begin the brewfestivities. In addition to the usual fun in Ironforge and Orgrimmar, you can complete new Brewfest quests throughout Quel’Thalas, and the Brewfest Banquet Outdoor Scenario will keep you hopping.

What's Brewfest without some stout rewards? Head over to our article to see what's freshly tapped for Midnight.
